<module id="sequence_detector">
    <description>A sequence detector to detect the specific 4-bit binary sequence 1001.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">The clock signal to synchronize the detector.</input>
        <input id="reset_n">The active-low reset signal to initialize the state machine.</input>
        <input id="data_in">A 1-bit binary input signal representing the next bit in the bitstream.</input>
        <output id="sequence_detected">A 1-bit output signal indicating whether the specific sequence has been detected.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">Waiting for the start of the sequence.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S1">First bit of the desired sequence detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S2">Second bit of the desired sequence detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S3">Third bit of the desired sequence detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S4">Fourth and final bit of the desired sequence detected.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="current_state" width_description="[2:0]">Register to hold the current state of the state machine.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" width_description="[2:0]">Register to hold the next state of the state machine.</reg>
        
        <always @(posedge clk or posedge reset_n)>
            if (reset_n == 1'b1)
                current_state <= IDLE;
            else
                current_state <= next_state;
        </always>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Define the state machine states
        parameter IDLE = 3'b000;
        parameter S1 = 3'b001;
        parameter S2 = 3'b010;
        parameter S3 = 3'b011;
        parameter S4 = 3'b100;
        // Define the state machine outputs
        reg [2:0] current_state, next_state;
        // Define the sequence detector logic
        always @(posedge clk or posedge reset_n) begin
            if (reset_n == 1'b1) begin
                current_state <= IDLE;
            end else begin
                current_state <= next_state;
            end
        end
        
        always @(*) begin
            case(current_state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1)
                        next_state = S1;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                S1: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0)
                        next_state = S2;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                S2: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0)
                        next_state = S3;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                S3: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1)
                        next_state = S4;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                S4: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1)
                        next_state = IDLE;
                    else
                        next_state = IDLE;
                end
                
                default: next_state = IDLE;
            endcase
        end
        
        // Output the sequence detected signal
        assign sequence_detected = (current_state == S4 && data_in == 1'b1);
    </implementation>
</module>
